# Incident Report: STRRAT Infection — Host 172.16.1.66

**Evidence:** `2024-07-30-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (11,562 frames, 11.5 MB, ~511 sec capture). No separate IDS/Suricata alert files were present in the evidence directory; findings below are derived entirely from packet analysis via tshark.

## Infected Host

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 address | 172.16.1.66 |
| MAC address | 00:1e:64:ec:f3:08 (Intel) |
| Windows hostname | DESKTOP-SKBR25F |
| AD domain | wiresharkworkshop.online |
| Logged-in user | ccollier |
| OS (self-reported by malware) | Microsoft Windows 11 Pro, 64-bit |

Confirmed via NBNS name registration (`DESKTOP-SKBR25F<00>/<20>`), Kerberos AS-REQ CNameString (`ccollier`, `DESKTOP-SKBR25F$`), and ARP (172.16.1.66 → 00:1e:64:ec:f3:08). Domain controller: WIRESHARK-WS-DC at 172.16.1.4 (MAC 5c:f9:dd:8c:97:35).

## Malware Family

**STRRAT** (Java-based RAT/credential stealer). **Signature-confirmed**, not behavioral inference — the malware's own C2 "ping" beacon contains the literal string `STRRAT` and version `1.6` in plaintext (TCP, unencrypted, no TLS):

```
ping|STRRAT|1BE8292C|DESKTOP-SKBR25F|ccollier|Microsoft Windows 11 Pro|64-bit|Windows Defender|<base64 window title>|1.6|US:United States|Not Installed|<uptime>
```

- Bot/campaign ID: `1BE8292C`
- Beacon interval: ~5 seconds
- Reported AV: Windows Defender
- Reported keylogger status: "Not Installed"
- First beacon: t=76.99s (TCP SYN); last observed beacon: t≈310s (5 min 10 sec uptime field)
- Base64 window-title fields decoded: `SG9tZQ==` = "Home", `UHJvZ3JhbSBNYW5hZ2Vy` = "Program Manager" (desktop foreground window telemetry)

## Indicators of Compromise

**Command and control**
- `141.98.10.79:12132` — TCP, plaintext STRRAT ping protocol. This is the only external connection observed on a non-standard port; every other outbound session from the host used 443 (TLS) or 80 (HTTP). No DNS lookup preceded this connection — the C2 IP is hardcoded in the sample.

**Suspicious/reconnaissance HTTP**
- `hxxp://ip-api.com/json/` (208.95.112.1:80) at t=78.0s — GET `/json/` with a static `Chrome/73.0.3683.86` user-agent inconsistent with the rest of the host's traffic. Classic malware self-geolocation check, occurring ~1 second after the STRRAT beacon started. Response: HTTP 200, `application/json`, 294 bytes.

**Likely payload/dependency staging (TLS-encrypted, delivery infrastructure only — file names/hashes not recoverable from ciphertext)**
- `github.com` (140.82.113.3:443) — queried/connected at t≈64.0s
- `objects.githubusercontent.com` (185.199.110.133:443, also resolved 185.199.109/111/108.133) — 833 KB transferred, t≈64.8–70.9s
- `repo1.maven.org` (199.232.196.209:443, also resolved 199.232.192.209) — 8.9 MB transferred, t≈68.0–73.8s (largest single flow in the capture, consistent with a bundled JRE/loader fetch)
- `javadl-esd-secure.oracle.com` (23.194.164.136:443) — queried/connected at t≈340s

These three domains were contacted in the same ~10-second window immediately preceding the first C2 beacon and ip-api.com lookup, consistent with STRRAT's known behavior of fetching a portable Java runtime and/or loader stage before beaconing. No plaintext HTTP file transfer was captured for these sessions (all TLS), so **no file names or SHA256 hashes can be grounded in this traffic** — exporting HTTP/SMB objects from the pcap yielded only two legitimate items (`connecttest.txt` from `www.msftconnecttest.com`, and the `ip-api.com` JSON response) and standard Group Policy files (`GptTmpl.inf`, `Registry.pol`, `gpt.ini`) from SYSVOL, none of which are malicious.

**No malicious domain was DNS-resolved** for the C2 IP itself (141.98.10.79) — it was contacted directly by hardcoded IP, which is itself an IOC (absence of a corresponding DNS query for an active outbound session on a non-standard port).

## Summary

DESKTOP-SKBR25F (172.16.1.66, user ccollier) retrieved staging content from github.com/objects.githubusercontent.com and repo1.maven.org around t=64–74s, then began beaconing to a STRRAT C2 server at 141.98.10.79:12132 over plaintext TCP starting at t=77s, alongside an IP-geolocation lookup to ip-api.com. The beacon persisted every ~5 seconds through the end of the capture (~t=310s+), self-identifying as STRRAT v1.6, bot ID 1BE8292C, with no keylogger flagged as installed at time of capture.
